These give materially different numbers from the same physical situation.
Reading (a) is assumed below because it is the most common convention in

Consequence: this figure is used as a CROSS-CHECK, never as a model input.
The default receptivity in energy.py is unchanged by it.

regeneration_squeeze.quantity_ja: 回生絞り込み / 回生失効
description: When line voltage rises because no nearby train is drawing current, the
supply suppresses regeneration to protect equipment, and the energy is
lost. This is the physical mechanism behind the receptivity parameter.
JR East reports investigating reduced substation reference feeding voltage
specifically to make squeeze less likely.
regeneration_squeeze.relevance: Confirms that receptivity is a real operational variable rather than a modelling convenience, and that it is not fixed -- the operator actively works to raise it.
